absent: Almost entirely European, and almost entirely white political theory: no Fals Borda or Latin American PAR, no Santos or ecology of knowledges, no Tsing or Juarrero. Conde (2022) on unsettling coloniality is the single decolonial entry in 79 references, so agonism arrives here as Mouffe's argument rather than as a conversation with Southern traditions that theorised conflict in participation first.
forYou: This is the clearest available answer to the problem your ecosystems work keeps hitting: what to do when stakeholders genuinely disagree and consensus methods paper over it. The reflexive-evaluation apparatus (Regeer, Van Mierlo, Verwoerd) is Dutch, close to home, and directly transferable to how you evaluate the CDC Urban Innovation course and Digital Twin Flevoland - and agonism is a sharper tool than 'enabling constraints' for the conflict half of 'Substrate Matters'.
method: References from Crossref; strands and narrative by Claude, grounded only in the reference list and title.
narrative:
The oldest root is unglamorous: Parks (1981) on citizens as co-producers of public services, picked up by Verschuere (2012) and Bryson (2017). Alongside it runs the sustainability-science line from Cash (2003) through Bremer (2017), Lemos (2018), Miller (2020) and Norstrom (2020), which by Chambers (2021, 2022) had hardened into principles and modes. Durose (2022) and Verwoerd (2023) mark the point where that literature starts asking whether co-production is a good concept at all.

The critical counter-current is just as long. Cooke (2003) on participation as the new tyranny, Klenk (2015) on the integration imperative, Jordan (2016) on neoliberalism in PAR, Delvenne (2020), Turnhout (2020), Carr (2021) on institutional ceremonies and Struminska-Kutra (2022) on taking power seriously all say the same thing in different registers: participation can absorb dissent rather than act on it. The paper's answer is Mouffe (2000, 2013). Agonistic pluralism is recent in this field - Koutsouris (2022) brought it to education, Chivers (2025) and Popa (2025) to policy and technology governance - so the paper is working a thin and current seam.

Underneath both sits a specifically Dutch methodological apparatus: reflexive monitoring in action (Van Mierlo, 2010), dynamic learning agendas (van Veen, 2014) and the Natuurpact reflexive evaluations (Verwoerd, 2019, 2020, 2021; Brouwers, 2022), with Regeer (2011, 2024) framing transdisciplinarity for transformation. Zuiderent-Jerak's own STS lineage - Jasanoff (1996), Callon (2005), situated intervention (2015), Laurent (2016), Lezaun (2017) - supplies the idea that the evaluator is inside the experiment, not outside judging it.
